title: 行宫
author: 元稹
intro: An abandoned palace, flowers blooming red for no one, and a few white-haired palace women sitting idle, talking about an emperor long dead. Twenty characters hold the rise and fall of a dynasty.
analysis: 行宫是皇帝外出时住的宫殿。这首诗写一座冷冷清清的旧行宫：皇帝早就不来了，宫里的花还是照样开得红红的，却没有人欣赏，所以说“寂寞红”。宫里还剩几位头发全白的老宫女，她们年轻时被选进宫，一辈子关在这里，如今闲坐着，说起当年唐玄宗时候的事。唐玄宗在位时是唐朝最繁华的“开元盛世”，后来发生安史之乱，国家由盛转衰。诗人只写了一座宫、一片花、几个老人，什么评论也没有，可是“红”花和“白”头的对比、过去的热闹和现在的冷清，让读者自己去体会。这种用很少的字写很深的意思，叫“言有尽而意无穷”。古人称赞它二十个字就写尽了一个王朝的兴衰。
analysisEn: A xínggōng is a palace where the emperor stayed when travelling. This poem shows one long abandoned: no emperor has come for years, yet the palace flowers still bloom red — with no one to look at them, so they are “lonely red”. A few palace women remain, their hair now white. They were chosen for the palace when young and spent their whole lives shut up there; now they sit idle, talking about the days of Emperor Xuanzong. His reign was the Tang dynasty’s golden age, until the An Lushan Rebellion (755–763) sent the empire into decline. The poet shows only a palace, some flowers and a few old women, and adds no comment at all. The contrast of red flowers and white heads, of past splendour and present emptiness, is left for us to feel. Saying a great deal with very few words — “the words end, the meaning goes on” — is an ideal of Chinese poetry, and old critics praised this poem for telling a dynasty’s rise and fall in twenty characters.
background: Yuan Zhen (779–831), a Tang official and poet and close friend of Bai Juyi, wrote this decades after Emperor Xuanzong’s reign (712–756). The palace is often identified as the Shangyang Palace in Luoyang, where palace women were sent to live out their lives, though this is not certain.
pronunciation: 行宫 xíng gōng（不读 háng）；寥落 liáo luò。
version: 采用通行教材文本，各版本基本无异文。

lines.en: The old travelling palace stands deserted;

lines.lit: the palace flowers are lonely red.
lines.en: its flowers bloom red, with no one to see.
A few white-haired palace women still remain,

lines.lit: idly sitting, they talk of Xuanzong.
lines.en: sitting idle, talking of the old emperor’s days.

words.en: a travelling palace (for an emperor’s journeys)
words.note: 皇帝出行时住的宫殿；“行”读 xíng。今天的“承德避暑山庄”也是一座行宫。
书面语，现代汉语说“冷清”“空荡荡”。
现代汉语也常用；这里写花“寂寞”，是拟人。
现代汉语说“白发”；成语“白头偕老”还用。
在宫中服侍皇家的女子，今天只用于讲历史。
现代汉语说“闲着坐着”；“闲”= 没事做。
唐玄宗李隆基，在位时有“开元盛世”，后期发生安史之乱。

imagery.name: 宫阙
imagery.zh: 冷清的旧行宫，是唐朝由盛到衰的见证。
imagery.en: The deserted old palace is a silent witness to the Tang dynasty’s fall from glory.

imagery.name: 花
imagery.zh: 宫花年年照样红，却没人看，以花的热闹反衬宫的冷清。
imagery.en: The flowers bloom red every year with no one to see them — their brightness makes the palace feel emptier.

imagery.name: 白发
imagery.zh: 宫女的白头说明时间过去了几十年，她们的青春都耗在了宫里；“白”与“红”形成对比。
imagery.en: The women’s white hair shows decades gone by and youth spent behind palace walls; white sets off the red of the flowers.
